definitions.gloss: to feel dizzy; to have one's head spin
definitions.explanation: A physical sensation of dizziness or vertigo, as if things are spinning around.

definitions.gloss: to be extremely busy; to be swamped
definitions.explanation: Figuratively describes being so overwhelmed with work or tasks that one's head spins.

examples.japanese: ⟦{急|きゅう}→急：13042_kyuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}ったら→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧{目|め}が{回|まわ}った。
examples.english: I felt dizzy when I stood up suddenly.

examples.japanese: ⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦ところ→ところ：01137_tokoro⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{下|した}→下：00670_shita⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{目|め}が{回|まわ}る。
examples.english: Looking down from a high place makes me dizzy.

examples.japanese: ⟦{乗|の}り{物酔|ものよ}い→乗り物酔い：25234_norimonoyoi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{目|め}が{回|まわ}って、⟦{歩|ある}けなかった→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: I was so dizzy from motion sickness that I couldn't walk.

examples.english: The end of the year is dizzyingly busy.

examples.english: Orders are flooding in and I'm swamped.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}し⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧やら⟦{手続|てつづ}き→手続き：05453_tetsuzuki⟧やらで、{目|め}が{回|まわ}るような⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧だ。
examples.english: Between moving preparations and paperwork, every day is a whirlwind.

notes:
A common idiomatic expression using the body part ⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧ (eye). The literal image of eyes spinning works for both physical dizziness and figurative overwhelm. Sense 2 often appears in the pattern {目|め}が{回|まわ}るほど⟦{忙|いそが}しい→忙しい：00591_isogashii⟧ (so busy one's head spins).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {目|め}が{回|まわ}るほど: to the point of dizziness; extremely (busy, etc.)
- {目|め}が{回|まわ}るような{忙|いそが}しさ: dizzying busyness

SIMILAR WORDS:
- めまい⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to feel dizzy — more clinical/medical
- ⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦くらくら→くらくら：06758_kurakura⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: head is spinning — more casual
- ⟦{猫|ねこ}の{手|て}も{借|か}りたい→猫の手も借りたい：06215_nekonotemokaritai⟧: so busy one would borrow a cat's paws — idiomatic for extreme busyness
